title: Dressed for Celebration
description: During Dia de los Muertos celebrations, women and girls in Mexico commonly dress as the famous skeletal figure known as La Catrina. In the early 1900s, artist José Guadalupe Posada created the character to satirize Mexicans who embraced European customs—a figure cloaked in European clothes, while its "bones" remain Mexican. Later popularized by artist Diego Rivera, La Catrina is the most recognizable symbol of the holiday and embodies Mexican identity.
translated_description: 在亡灵节庆祝活动中，墨西哥的女性与女孩通常会装扮成著名的骷髅形象“拉·卡特里娜”。20世纪初，艺术家何塞·瓜达卢佩·波萨达创作了这个角色，用以讽刺那些崇尚欧洲习俗的墨西哥人——这个人物披着欧式服装，而它的“骨头”仍是墨西哥的。后来经艺术家迭戈·里维拉推广，拉·卡特里娜成为该节日最具辨识度的象征，并体现了墨西哥人的身份认同。
